overview: Greentown Management is China's largest capital-light, third-party real estate project-management ("daijian"/construction agency) company, managing residential and other developments on behalf of asset owners (private developers, state-owned enterprises, urban investment companies/LGFVs, government bodies and capital investors) in exchange for project management fees, rather than owning land or housing inventory itself. Spun off from Greentown China (3900.HK) and listed on HKEX in July 2020 as the first pure-play project-management stock in China, it has held a market share above 20% for ten consecutive years (FY2016-FY2025) across 132 cities in 31 provinces. The ultimate controlling shareholder chain runs through Greentown China to China Communications Construction Group (CCCC), a central state-owned enterprise, which the company increasingly leans on for brand/credit endorsement and (nascent) overseas expansion resources.

business_model.summary: Greentown Management earns project management fees (typically a percentage of project sales value/cost, or fixed fees) for managing the design, construction, marketing and delivery of real estate projects on behalf of asset owners, without deploying its own balance sheet capital into land or construction inventory. This is a capital-light, high-ROE, fee-for-service model, structurally different from a traditional developer. Revenue is project-and-milestone based (recognized over time as services are rendered) rather than purely recurring, though the large multi-year order backlog (120 million sqm on hand as of H1 FY2026) gives several years of revenue visibility. Historically revenue was split into three reporting lines -- commercial project management, government project management, and other (consulting/supply-chain) services -- but FY2025 disclosure simplified this to "project management services" (98.3% of revenue) vs "other services" (1.7%), reflecting the declining relevance of pure government-mandated project management.

revenue_streams.name: Commercial project management (self-operated + JV with partners)
revenue_streams.trend: growing (FY2024), now folded into combined 'project management services' line which fell 9.3% in FY2025

revenue_streams.name: Government project management (incl. affordable-housing/distressed-project rescue mandates)
revenue_streams.trend: declining sharply -- down 20.6% in FY2024 as policy-driven demand (bailout/guaranteed-delivery mandates) winds down

revenue_streams.name: Other services (consulting, supply chain, pre-listing legacy projects)

business_model.customer_type: B2B/B2G -- private developers, state-owned developers, local-government urban investment companies (LGFVs), municipal housing authorities, and increasingly "capital-owner" (financial investor) clients seeking an operating partner for land they already hold
business_model.geographic_mix: 100% Mainland China operations, RMB-denominated; projects spread across 31 provinces/132 cities with increasing concentration in Tier-1/Tier-2 cities and the four major city clusters (76.5% of on-hand order book as of H1 FY2026); dividends declared in RMB and paid in HKD

main_competitors: Jindi/Sunac and other developer-spun-off project-management units
Local/regional project management boutiques and in-house developer project-management teams
competitive_position.market_position: Industry leader by scale for 10 consecutive years with >20% market share (ranked No.1 in 8 of the top 10 provincial markets in FY2025); only an estimated ~30 active enterprises nationally retain full customer-acquisition and operational capability, with smaller players being eliminated -- the sector is consolidating around a handful of scaled leaders including Greentown and CCMGT

moat_factors.description: The 'Greentown' brand connotes premium product quality ("good housing" standard, 'Greentown Star' standards) and commands fee premiums -- 60% of newly contracted projects in H1 FY2026 carried fee rates above 3%, above industry averages

Indirect backing from China Communications Construction Group (a central SOE) via parent Greentown China lends credibility with government and LGFV clients and lowers perceived counterparty/execution risk versus privately-owned project managers

Delivered >10 million sqm annually for five consecutive years with high owner satisfaction (92-98 points); large, geographically diversified backlog (120 million sqm) reduces single-project concentration risk

Client repeat-mandate rate rose to ~25-26% in FY2025/H1 FY2026 (up from lower levels), indicating increasing but still modest stickiness; project management contracts are generally one-off/per-project rather than evergreen
No bank borrowings, high cash balance (~RMB1.4bn), low gearing (~1%), giving resilience through the property downturn relative to balance-sheet developers

weaknesses: Low switching costs/barriers to entry for smaller competitors mean intense fee-rate competition; industry-wide fee rates have been compressed as the market became a 'buyer's market'
Revenue and margins are directly exposed to the broader China real estate down-cycle (new contract volumes, land acquisition by clients) despite the capital-light model
Government/LGFV project-management revenue has swung sharply (-20.6% FY2024) as policy support (affordable housing repurchase, guaranteed-delivery programs) phases out
Heavy reliance on a cyclical, policy-sensitive end market with limited geographic diversification outside Mainland China (overseas expansion is nascent/exploratory)
Gross margin compressed materially -- from 49.6% (FY2024) to 39.7% (FY2025) -- indicating the moat is not fully protecting profitability in a down industry

growth_drivers: Revitalization of urban investment companies' (LGFV) undeveloped land bank -- estimated at 340-400 million sqm nationally -- seen as a multi-year structural demand source for project management services

Urban renewal (old neighborhood renovation, urban village redevelopment, historic district revitalization) -- a RMB20 trillion opportunity over the next five years per management, and a 'Fifteenth Five-Year Plan' policy priority

'Capital-owner' (资方代建) project management -- a new, still-exploratory model where financial investors/capital owners partner with developers and need an independent operator; management frames this as a new growth curve
Rising industry penetration rate and geographic expansion from the Yangtze River Delta heartland into third- and fourth-tier cities and new regions nationally
Non-residential/urban comprehensive service expansion (industrial parks, schools, talent apartments) diversifying beyond pure residential project management
Nascent overseas project management exploration leveraging parent CCCC's overseas resource network
Industry consolidation ('Matthew effect') concentrating share with the few full-cycle-capable leaders (including Greentown) as marginal competitors exit
AI/digital transformation initiatives aimed at cost control, design/engineering efficiency and margin protection under the new 'Strategy 2030' plan

business.description: New contract volumes for the whole project-management industry fell 8.2% YoY in H1 FY2026 as developer/LGFV land acquisition and new housing starts keep declining; multi-year contraction in the addressable market
Industry-wide tightening of commercial terms and declining project management fee rates as the market becomes a 'buyer's market'; gross margin fell from 49.6% to 39.7% in one year

Policy-driven government project management (bailout/guaranteed-delivery, affordable-housing repurchase mandates) is winding down, removing what had been a meaningful, higher-margin-adjacent revenue pool

Clients are real-estate developers and LGFVs, many financially stressed in the current downturn; fee collection depends on clients' own cash flow and solvency, and trade receivables/contract assets (combined ~RMB2.6bn) represent meaningful working-capital and collection risk even though Greentown itself holds no project inventory

business.risk: Product/service obsolescence as market shifts to stock (existing-home) cycle
business.description: Management itself flags that new-build project management is contracting while second-hand home transactions have overtaken new-home sales for the first time (H1 FY2026) -- the company must prove its model extends profitably into urban renewal/existing-stock operations, which are less proven commercially

financial.description: FY2025 net profit attributable to owners fell 47.7% YoY, driven partly by non-operating items including a RMB72.5m intangible asset impairment and increases in contingent consideration payable on a prior acquisition (Zhejiang Greentown Shangli)

Business and reporting are in RMB but dividends are declared in RMB and paid in HKD; company does not hedge FX exposure and RMB depreciation/appreciation can affect reported HKD dividend value for international holders
Contract assets rose 14.7% YoY to RMB1,541.8m at FY2025 end, reflecting fees earned but not yet billable/collectible -- a cash-flow timing risk tied to client solvency

regulatory.description: Government project management revenue is directly exposed to central/local policy changes (affordable housing programs, guaranteed-delivery initiatives); policy withdrawal already caused a 20.6% revenue decline in this segment in FY2024

regulatory.risk: Land and local government debt policy
regulatory.description: A large structural growth driver (LGFV land revitalization) depends on local government debt resolution policy and fiscal capacity, which are themselves subject to Beijing's deleveraging agenda

macro.risk: China real estate down-cycle / consumer demand
macro.description: National real estate development investment and new commercial housing sales continued to decline YoY in H1 FY2026; project management is indirectly but materially exposed via clients' willingness and ability to launch new projects

macro.risk: Macro growth and credit conditions in China
macro.description: Broader Chinese economic growth, local government fiscal stress and credit availability to developers/LGFVs affect both new contract volume and fee collection timeliness
Reliance on policy-driven demand pools (affordable housing, urban renewal funding) that could be slower to materialize than management's RMB20 trillion five-year urban renewal estimate implies

execution.description: Board chairmanship changed twice within about 15 months -- Zhang Yadong resigned March 2025, Geng Zhongqiang became Co-Chairman then sole Chairman (March 2026), then Geng resigned and Zhao Hui was appointed Chairman effective 31 July 2026 -- alongside auditor change from Ernst & Young to KPMG (effective June 2026), indicating a period of governance/organizational flux concurrent with the parent group's own CEO change at Greentown China

execution.risk: New business model execution (capital-owner project management, overseas expansion)
execution.description: Management describes 'capital-owner' project management and overseas project management as still in an 'exploration stage' -- these are unproven revenue models that the bull case partly depends on

macro_factors.industry_outlook: China's project management ('daijian') industry is in a multi-year structural adjustment: newly contracted scale fell 8.2% YoY in H1 FY2026 after two consecutive years of market-size contraction, but industry penetration of China's real estate market is still rising, and management/third-party estimates point to large medium-term opportunities in LGFV land revitalization (~340-400m sqm nationally) and urban renewal (~RMB20 trillion market over 5 years). Industry has shifted from scale-growth competition to profitability/service-quality competition, with roughly 30 nationally capable competitors remaining and smaller players exiting.
macro_factors.cyclicality: High -- directly linked to the China residential real estate cycle (new contract signings track developer/LGFV land acquisition and new housing starts), though the capital-light, fee-based model and lack of balance-sheet inventory risk provide materially more downside protection than a traditional developer would have
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Indirect but meaningful -- Chinese mortgage rates and developer financing costs drive end-buyer demand and client willingness to launch new projects, which in turn drives new contract volume and fee realization for Greentown
key_input_costs: Skilled project-management and engineering headcount (labor costs are described as 'rigid' and a margin pressure point)
IT/digital transformation and AI tooling spend
Marketing/sales expenses tied to project launches

recent_developments.event: Mr. Zhao Hui appointed Chairman of the Board effective 31 July 2026, succeeding Mr. Geng Zhongqiang (a long-time China Communications Construction Group executive), who resigned the same date
Shareholders approved KPMG as new auditor, replacing Ernst & Young, effective from the AGM on 26 June 2026 (E&Y itself had replaced Deloitte in 2024)

Revenue of RMB1.466bn, up 7% YoY; net profit attributable to owners RMB271m, up 6% YoY; gross margin improved to 41%; operating cash flow RMB134m, up 20% YoY; new contract GFA 13.52m sqm with RMB3.41bn of new project management fees; interim dividend of RMB0.076/share declared (second consecutive year of interim dividend)
Mr. Cheng Min appointed Executive Director (previously VP responsible for capital-owner/资方代建 project management); Ms. Nie Huanxin (Chief Digital Officer) appointed to the Nomination Committee

Revenue fell 9.3% YoY to RMB3,120.1m; gross margin fell sharply from 49.6% to 39.7%; net profit attributable to owners fell 47.7% to RMB419.0m, partly due to intensifying industry fee-rate competition and non-operating impairments/fair-value losses; proposed final + special dividend of RMB0.1335/share combined; first share buyback completed, cancelling 10 million shares (~HK$30.7m) in October 2025

Board co-chairman structure introduced (April 2025) then consolidated into a single Chairman role held by Mr. Geng Zhongqiang (March 2026), reflecting closer integration with Greentown China/CCCC group governance

Management launched 'Strategy 2030' with a comprehensive business review, emphasizing AI/digital transformation, organizational/incentive reform, cost discipline (admin + S&M expenses down 7% YoY in H1 FY2026) and exploration of overseas project management leveraging CCCC's international footprint

guidance.as_of: H1 FY2026 Interim Report (six months ended 30 June 2026) and FY2025 Annual Report

items.target: over 10 million sqm (expects to deliver an additional 9.5 million sqm / ~47,000 units in H2 FY2026, on top of 5.456 million sqm delivered in H1)
items.notes: Would mark the sixth consecutive year delivering more than 10 million sqm annually

items.target: no less than 80% of net profit attributable to owners (including interim dividend)
items.notes: Subject to operating results, working capital needs, capex plans and board/shareholder approval; FY2025 actual full-year payout (final + special + interim) was already substantial, and interim dividend was paid for a second consecutive year in H1 FY2026

items.target: continue raising proportion of new contracted fees from Tier-1/Tier-2 cities (64.3% in H1 FY2026) and maintain >60% of new projects with fee rates above 3%
items.notes: Framed as a profitability 'safety cushion' strategy rather than a hard numeric target

items.target: No explicit numeric full-year FY2026 revenue or profit guidance given
items.notes: Management commentary is qualitative: expects short-term industry pressure to persist (new contract scale down 8.2% YoY industry-wide in H1 FY2026) but describes H1 FY2026 operating fundamentals as 'stable' with 'improving profit quality' and 'enhanced financial resilience'

guidance.management_commentary: Management (new Chairman Zhao Hui and CEO Wang Junfeng) characterizes the real estate industry's adjustment cycle as ongoing but says the project-management sector's medium-to-long-term structural opportunities (LGFV land revitalization, urban renewal, affordable housing) remain intact, and that leading, full-cycle-capable, well-capitalized players like Greentown will keep taking share as smaller competitors exit ('Matthew effect'). The company frames FY2026 as the launch year of 'Strategy 2030', emphasizing capability-building, AI/digital tooling, cost discipline and shareholder returns (dividend payout commitment) over top-line growth, given a genuinely contracting near-term addressable market.

bull_case: Clear #1 market position (>20% share for 10 straight years) in a capital-light, high-return business model that is far more resilient than balance-sheet developers through the China property downturn -- no bank debt, ~RMB1.4bn net cash, strong free cash flow generation

Large multi-year revenue visibility from a 120 million sqm order backlog, with increasing mix shift toward higher-quality, higher-fee-rate Tier-1/Tier-2 city projects (64.3% of new contracts in H1 FY2026, fee rate >3% on 60% of new projects)

Structural, multi-trillion-RMB long-term demand pools (LGFV land revitalization ~340-400m sqm, urban renewal ~RMB20tn over 5 years) that play directly to Greentown's project-management expertise as China shifts from new-build to existing-stock development
Strong, high-payout-ratio dividend policy (targeting ≥80% of net profit) offering an attractive yield (reported ~12% forward yield by some trackers) while the company waits out the cycle

Deepening SOE/central-government linkage via parent Greentown China's largest shareholder, China Communications Construction Group, which lends credibility with government/LGFV clients and could open overseas project-management opportunities
bear_case: Revenue and profit are in clear decline -- FY2025 revenue down 9.3% and net profit attributable to owners down 47.7% YoY, with gross margin collapsing from 49.6% to 39.7% as industry-wide fee-rate competition intensifies

The addressable market itself is shrinking: project management industry new-contract scale fell again in H1 FY2026 (-8.2% YoY) after two prior years of contraction, driven by the broader China real estate downturn and reduced LGFV/government land acquisition

Government project management -- previously ~18% of revenue -- is structurally declining as policy-driven mandates (affordable housing repurchase, guaranteed-delivery rescue projects) wind down, removing a revenue pool with no clear like-for-like replacement yet proven at scale
Growth narratives (capital-owner project management, overseas expansion, urban renewal monetization) are explicitly described by management as still exploratory/early-stage, not yet revenue-material

Governance churn -- two chairman changes and an auditor change within roughly 18 months -- adds execution-risk uncertainty at exactly the time the company is trying to execute a strategic pivot ('Strategy 2030') in a difficult industry environment
